name: Ghenh Rang
kicker: Egg stones and the queen’s cove
summary: Walk the egg-shaped stones the sea has rounded, about 3 km southeast of the center. The portal calls the cove bãi tắm Hoàng Hậu because Nam Phương Hoàng Hậu bathed here. The visit is free. This is not the city crescent, and it is not Bãi Xếp, 13 km further south.
getThere: About 3 km southeast of the center. Minutes are check on arrival.
heroCaption: Egg-shaped stones along the water at Ghềnh Ráng

notice.title: The queen’s cove is bãi tắm Hoàng Hậu
notice.body: An English map that says Queen will not use the portal’s name. The cove is bãi tắm Hoàng Hậu, on this rock coast. Bãi Xếp, 13 km south, is a different village, and its fee is check on arrival.

body: The portal names egg-shaped stones the sea has rounded, a Vọng Phu rock, a lion-shaped rock, bãi tắm Tiên Sa, and Hàn Mặc Tử’s grave on the hillside. It says Bảo Đại chose Ghềnh Ráng as a royal retreat from 1927. From the grave, that page says you see the east of the city and Phương Mai.
The church page puts the area about 3 km southeast of the center. The visit field is 60 minutes and the open field is 7:00–18:00. The fee is free. Minutes from the beach are check on arrival.

figures.caption: Hàn Mặc Tử’s monument on the hillside, full figure
figures.alt: The white figure of Hàn Mặc Tử on a stone pedestal above the grave at Ghềnh Ráng

gettingThere: The stone-church page says Ghềnh Ráng is about 3 km southeast of the center, in Phường Quy Nhơn Nam. Minutes are check on arrival.
Bãi Xếp is 13 km south on the Quy Nhơn–Sông Cầu road. It is not this cove.

legs.heading: From the center
legs.body: About 3 km southeast. The portal does not print the minutes. Check on arrival.

closed: No weekly closing day is printed.
